problem: Existing language-conditioned robotics work maps language to rewards (safety as a soft cost), and the few language-to-safety methods handle only narrow constraint classes (e.g., obstacle avoidance) or need heavy domain-specific engineering. Classical safety filters (MPC, CBF, HJ reachability) assume fixed, precomputed constraints.
motivation: Robots in human-centered spaces must obey context- and user-dependent semantic safety constraints (e.g., 'be quiet near the bed', 'don't go under the standing desk') that cannot be anticipated a priori but are easily expressed in language. Enforcing them at runtime requires grounding vague instructions in perception, generalizing across constraint types, keeping specifications interpretable, and running in real time.
key_idea: Parse free-form safety instructions with an LLM into JSON constraint templates, ground them as object-level 3D/2D semantic failure sets via fused CLIP and panoptic segmentation, and enforce them together with geometric constraints using a sampling-based MPC safety filter.
insight: Modularity with an interpretable template lets one framework cover spatial exclusion, kinematic modulation and abstract intent constraints. Fusing CLIP segmentation with panoptic boundaries gives tighter failure sets: the Safe-Lang baseline, with its over-conservative masks, suffers many perception timeouts, while Safe-Geom fails semantic constraints altogether. Sampling-based filters are flexible enough for dynamically generated constraints; smooth-blending helps pace-modulation tasks but costs more latency (10 ms vs 2 ms).
method: Language module: GPT-4o with a fixed prompt, schema and few-shot examples translates each instruction into a JSON config {type, obj, buffer, vel max, angular vel max}; it asks for clarification when instructions are ambiguous, and the active list is capped at M entries.

Constraint classes: spatial exclusion (enter/beneath/buffer), kinematic modulation (speed limits, possibly context-conditioned), and abstract intent (resolved by the LLM into exclusion or modulation primitives).

Perception module: ClipSeg open-vocabulary masks are fused with Mask2Former panoptic regions (keeping regions whose IoU with the CLIP mask exceeds a threshold); masked depth is projected into a per-constraint TSDF using 2D-LiDAR-SLAM pose, then into a 2D occupancy map.

Semantic failure set: each config maps to F_sem^i = {l_i(x) - buffer_i <= 0}, with l_i an SDF for exclusion, a velocity margin for modulation, and a max of the two for intent; the union over i is combined with the geometric failure set.

Safety score (SB-MPC): a sampling-based, MPPI-like solver of max over controls of min over the horizon of l(x_k), with N=50 samples and R=2 refinement iterations, warm-started from the previous sequence.
Least-restrictive filter: execute u_nom if its safety score exceeds epsilon=0.25, otherwise switch to the SB-MPC backup control.
Smooth-blending filter: from 25 control primitives keep those satisfying the CBF-inspired condition V_prim - V >= -gamma V (gamma=5), then choose the one closest to u_nom, falling back to SB-MPC.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) for parsing; ClipSeg + Mask2Former (pretrained, frozen) for perception; sampling-based MPC filter (no learning)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D + 2D LiDAR SLAM pose + odometry velocities
setting.action_space: low-level continuous controls [angular velocity, linear acceleration] of a 4D Dubins car, wrapped around an A* + PD nominal policy
setting.simulator: Habitat 3.0 (12 scenes) plus real TurtleBot 2 hardware
setting.privileged: in simulation, perfect state estimation and noise-free RGB-D/LiDAR; language instructions issued at t=0

numbers_note: Quantitative simulation results (success rate, semantic safety rate, timeout rates by constraint type) appear only in a figure (Fig. quantitative_results) with no numeric values in the text. Only the LLM parsing rate (52/60) and latencies are given in the text.
results: In 12 Habitat scenes with 5 trials per instruction, the method consistently achieves the best success and semantic safety rates versus Safe-Geom (very low semantic safety) and Safe-Lang (over-conservative masks, high timeouts). GPT-4o parsed 52 of 60 queries correctly, with the rest triggering clarification. On a TurtleBot 2 in a cluttered office, only the proposed method avoided going under the standing desk and reached the goal.
limitations: Failures propagate from ambiguous instructions, missed detections, odometry drift, and over-conservative segmentation causing the robot to freeze.
Safety is only discrete-time, deterministic, and not formally recursive (finite horizon, stochastic sampling); it does not model dynamics or perception uncertainty.
Perception and filtering latency can hurt responsiveness to suddenly appearing obstacles; evaluated on a small set (12 scenes, one hardware scenario, static environments), with no numeric tables.
builds_on: Safe-Lang (Santos et al., Updating Robot Safety Representations Online from Natural Language Feedback)
